What your result looks like

You receive not a single figure but two value ranges with reasoning. The values below are an invented example so you can see what to expect.

Fictitious example
Initial assessment

3-room period flat, 85 m², built around 1905

Value today
€410,000 – €450,000
Value after renovation
€495,000 – €540,000
Rough renovation cost range
€45,000 – €60,000
What determines the range
Location, condition of bathroom and electrics, floor level, comparable sales
Recommendation
Consider renovating before selling: added value exceeds the costs

All figures are invented and do not apply to any real property.

How the valuation works

From first contact to result, you speak to the same person. You can start online, by video or with an on-site viewing.

  1. 01

    Enquiry and appointment

    Form, call or video appointment. GRENFORD gets back to you personally and agrees the next step with you.

  2. 02

    On-site viewing

    Location, building fabric, specification and documents. Plus a look at what a renovation would change.

  3. 03

    Valuation

    The value today and the value after a renovation, with a rough cost range and benchmarked against comparable properties.

  4. 04

    Results in conversation

    Personal presentation of the results, in writing on request: the basis for your decision whether to sell, renovate or hold.

Frequently asked questions

What does the valuation cost?＋

The initial assessment is free of charge and without obligation. It does not create a mandate.

How quickly will I hear back?＋

GRENFORD will get back to you personally within 48 hours, by the route you chose in the last step: email, phone or video call.

Is this an automatically calculated value?＋

No. GRENFORD reads your details personally and assesses them against location, condition and comparable properties. You receive a value range and an explanation.

What does “value after renovation” mean?＋

In addition to today’s value, the assessment shows how a sensible renovation could affect the value, with a rough cost range. So you can see whether a project pays off before you obtain quotes.

Is the valuation a formal appraisal?＋

No. GRENFORD prepares a market-based assessment as the basis for selling, buying or renovating. Tax authorities, courts or the division of an estate usually require a market value appraisal under § 194 BauGB. On request, GRENFORD brings in a certified expert for this.

Which documents help?＋

Your details are enough for the initial assessment. For a precise valuation, the floor plan, living area calculation, energy performance certificate and, for let properties, the rent roll are helpful.

What happens to my details?＋

Your details are used exclusively to process your enquiry and are treated confidentially. You will find details in the privacy policy.
